name: lewm-residual-common-panel-20261030-v1
purpose: Implement diagnostics, residual mixture, common-panel selection and a bounded completion screen
mixture: One bounded network correction biases the last half (floor) of newly sampled candidates around the current CEM centre in each iteration, beginning at the native warm-start plan. Mean slot and retained archive unchanged; zero correction must reproduce native. Network evaluated once per replan. Same candidate population, iterations and feasibility checks.
information: Same 29 causal features as the first pilot. Privileged native task state supplies scalar training feedback only, never adapter inputs. No analytic predictor or simulator-preview checks. Full 15px pusher and 6px margin unchanged.
fitness: If any panel violation: -1000000 - number of violation episodes. Otherwise (n+1)*safe_completion_count + sum(safe_progress) - 0.001*capped_action_sum/(n*150). Successful episodes use actual actions, unfinished use 150. Completion dominates bounded progress; violations cannot be traded for task reward.
progress_feedback: Safe completion=1; unsafe or technical invalid=0; safe unfinished=clip(1-final_error/initial_error,0,1). Error=norm(goal[:4]-state[:4])/20 + shortest angular error/(pi/9). This uses privileged simulator task state for scalar training feedback, never as an adapter input. Future optimizer controls require the same information.
zero_initialization: Seeded hidden features, exactly zero output weights and bias. The untrained control uses seeded random output weights from the original network initializer.
panels: All generations and both optimizers use the identical four-case development panel. No raw-score comparison across different panels. CMA candidate order preseeded; random search draws the same number of independent candidates from initial+N(0,sigma), with the same panel, feedback, action and model-query caps.
nomination: CMA best common-panel score, ties earliest generation and candidate index. Random-search best score, ties earliest candidate. Never automatically deploy final CMA mean.
selection_rule: Compare native, zero, untrained, CMA elite and random-search elite on four fresh planner-seed cases. Highest common-panel fitness wins; exact ties follow listed arm order. Freeze receipt before any expansion.
influence_gate: Native and zero must have exactly equal actions, states and dense traces, plus equal model-query work on all diagnostic cases. Nonzero untrained residual must alter at least one action trace and enter at least one fitted elite set. Otherwise stop after nine diagnostic episodes.
completion_gate: CMA must have zero selection violations, strictly more safe completions than native, zero and untrained, and at least native engagement. This is a development signal, not a statistical or evolutionary advantage claim. Without it stop after 233 valid episodes and keep fresh-scene validation closed.
conditional_expansion: Only after a completion signal, prepare and freeze the next stage before its first episode: fresh start/goal scenes, repeated optimizer seeds and tuned-fixed/random/ordinary-learning controls with the same information and matched budgets. No expansion based on progress alone; no further rental or lease extension from this protocol.
stopping: Fixed frozen development schedule; retain ten minutes before rental cutoff for preservation. Stop on technical errors for diagnosis and preserve partial accounting. No outcome retry, outcome-based extra tuning, or altered safety settings. At most two failed technical starts count against total limits.
limitations: Development-only, one reused source scene and three known hazard layouts. Fresh planner seeds do not establish unseen-scene generalisation.
One CMA seed and one random-search seed. Matched candidate/panel caps do not imply equal actual environment or model work.
Ordinary learning and a new fixed-setting search are deferred until the completion gate. No evolutionary advantage claim is authorized by this development comparison.
